findings.F1: A coin's 24-hour return, scaled by its 30-day hourly volatility (z24), is followed by a graded reversal over the next 24 hours. On a non-overlapping 24-bar grid, the excess return in the fade direction is -0.06 % (t -1.2, n 7793) for |z24| ≤ 0.5, +0.07 % (t 0.9, n 4287) for 0.5–1, +0.46 % (t 4.7, n 2882) for 1–2, +0.61 % (t 2.2, n 602) for 2–3 and +1.73 % (t 3.1, n 219) above 3, and the pooled slope of the excess 24-hour return on z24 is -0.28 % per unit (t -6.9, n 15806).
findings.F2: This reversal holds on every coin separately, with 24-hour slopes of -0.16 % (BTC, t -2.3), -0.28 % (ETH, t -3.3), -0.25 % (LTC, t -2.4), -0.45 % (XMR, t -4.5), -0.27 % (XRP, t -2.4) and -0.32 % (ZEC, t -2.4), about 2650 cases each. By year the slope is negative in 7 of 8 years and has t ≤ -2.5 in 2018, 2019, 2021 and 2023; 2024 is the exception (+0.05 %, t 0.6).
findings.F3: The reversal belongs to a one-day horizon. At 12 hours the |z24| 1–2 bucket fades +0.19 % (t 3.6). At 48 hours no bucket reaches t 2, and at 72 hours none reaches t 1.5 (e.g. |z24| 1–2: +0.40 %, t 1.4), with no coin's 72-hour slope beyond |t| 1.4.
findings.F4: Among cases with |z24| > 1, the 24-hour fade grows with the ratio of 24-hour to 30-day volatility: +0.04 % (t 0.2, n 562) for a ratio below 0.8, +0.41 % (t 3.1, n 1485) for 0.8–1.2, +0.72 % (t 4.4, n 1334) for 1.2–2 and +1.46 % (t 3.0, n 322) above 2.
findings.F5: The reversal is larger after drops than after rises. With |z24| > 1, a 24-hour drop is followed by a +0.84 % excess rebound over 24 hours (t 5.7, n 1774), against a +0.30 % excess pullback after a rise (t 2.5, n 1929).
findings.F6: The tested 1-hour shock signal is small and not graded at its extremes.
findings.F7: The book's losses come from shorts held long. Short trades average -3.53 % before fees (5182 trades, 38 % winners) against +0.92 % for longs, and shorts held over 168 hours average -18.6 % (n 540). The book loses in 6 of 8 years, including -0.30 % a day in 2020 while the coins rose +0.42 % a day.

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's 24-hour return relative to its 30-day hourly volatility, the more its return over the next 24 hours runs the opposite way.
ideas.consequence: A trader would fade a coin's sharp one-day moves for one day, with a move per case several times the cost of a trade at the large end.
ideas.name: one-day move reverses next day

ideas.idea: The higher a coin's 24-hour volatility is relative to its 30-day volatility, the more its large 24-hour return, measured against its 30-day volatility, reverses over the next 24 hours.
ideas.consequence: A trader would fade one-day moves hardest when the day's volatility is far above its monthly norm, and refuse the fade when volatility is calm.
ideas.name: volatile-day move reversal

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's 24-hour drop relative to its 30-day hourly volatility, the larger its rise over the next 24 hours.
ideas.consequence: A trader would buy a coin after a sharp one-day fall for a one-day rebound, the side of the reversal that carries most of its size.
ideas.name: sharp daily drop rebounds
